subject: Benchmark plan, MAP milestones, and close timeline
messages:
From: Simon Bryant <simon.bryant@cloudretail.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Benchmark kickoff for CloudRetail POC

Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks for the sync earlier. As we start to formalize the MAP for the POC, a couple of asks from our side before we lock dates:

- Can you document the full performance plan (latency/throughput/TTFT and concurrency targets) and what tooling/harness you will use?
- We ran a quick pass this morning against the same open model and saw TTFTs that are ~30-40% higher than the numbers you shared in the demo. I want to avoid surprises in executive readouts.
- Our procurement timeline is tight — we need a go/no-go recommendation by the week of Aug 31 so we can commit budget.

If you can add a short MAP entry that ties each test to an acceptance criteria and a close date, that would help us align on scope. I attached a small CSV with the sample prompts and my team's run outputs.

Thanks,
Simon Bryant
Head of Platform
CloudRetail

Attachment: customer-kpi-sample.csv (CSV, 2 KB)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Simon Bryant <simon.bryant@cloudretail.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, nikhil_sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Benchmark kickoff for CloudRetail POC

Simon — appreciate the data and the ask. Attached is our initial MAP-performance-plan-v1 that binds benchmarks to acceptance criteria and an internal runbook. Summary here so the MAP is actionable for procurement: 

Goals (what we'll measure):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) measured from request receipt to first token on the wire — acceptance: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 320ms (50-token prompt baseline).
- Steady-state throughput: tokens/sec at 50 and 200 concurrent requests — acceptance: >= 18k tok/s at 50 conc, >= 55k tok/s at 200 conc (cluster-level).
- Latency distribution (p50/p90/p95) across 1, 8, 32 concurrency.
- Cold-start and KV-cache warm path comparisons.

Test harness and methodology:
- Redwood benchmark harness v2.1 (open-source runner + internal telemetry).
- We will run using the exact prompt set you provided (thanks) and also an anonymized 500-prompt stress set.
- Model variants: model-vX (float16), model-vX-q4 (4-bit quant) — we will provide both numbers, and a fallback profile (small-medium) if the high perf quantized variant shows degraded quality.
- Environment: dedicated Redwood cluster in us-west-2, same model weights we serve for hosted. Kernel/runtime: Redwood Serving Runtime v2.1 with continuous batching enabled.

Schedule (MAP milestones):
- Tue 2026-08-25: Run baseline internal tests, share raw CSVs.
- Thu 2026-08-27: Reproduce with customer's prompts and run joint canary (traceable with IDs).
- Mon 2026-08-30: Deliver final MAP summary + recommendation for close.

I've attached the MAP-performance-plan-v1.pdf with the acceptance criteria and a checklist for the joint run. We'll instrument traces so you can correlate our run IDs to your metrics.

Let me know if we should include any additional SLA numbers for the MAP. If this timeline works for procurement, we'll lock the Aug 30 close date.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: MAP-performance-plan-v1.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)

From: Simon Bryant <simon.bryant@cloudretail.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudRetail Eng Team <eng@cloudretail.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 10:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Benchmark kickoff for CloudRetail POC

Thanks Karthik — the plan looks solid. We ran the joint canary earlier today using our internal harness (Locust + internal RPC proxy) and attached the output. Highlights/concerns:

- Our TTFT (measured at edge) p50 = 165ms, p95 = 410ms on the same model-vX float16 baseline you listed. That delta is material to our UX team.
- We saw significantly higher p95 at concurrency 32 compared to your baseline. Our run used a 128-token response cap for safety.
- We are not using continuous batching on our side — calls are 1:1 from our proxy. Could that explain the TTFT gap (batching could increase TTFT but reduce cost)?

Attached the CSV with our runs (customer-kpi-sample.csv) and a short notes file describing the harness config. We requested that procurement keep the Aug 30 deadline, but the execs will want a short note on the discrepancy source.

Regards,
Simon

Attachment: customer-kpi-sample.csv (CSV, 8 KB)
Attachment: harness-config.txt (TXT, 1 KB)

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, nikhil_sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Benchmark kickoff for CloudRetail POC

Looping in a short triage runbook so we can quickly identify root causes for the discrepancy and keep the MAP timeline. Action items: 

1) Repro steps (owner: nikhil_sharma)	- Run Redwood harness v2.1 against customer's prompt set with: no batching (1:1), continuous batching on, and continuous batching off.	- Use same response cap (128 tokens) and same concurrency buckets (1,8,32).
2) Telemetry capture (owner: grace_oconnor)	- Export full tracer spans, include TTFT measurement points we define in the MAP doc (request-received, model-dequeue, first-token-sent).
3) Model parity (owner: marissa_cole)	- Validate checksum for model-vX weights and confirm quantized artifacts are identical to what we serve.
4) Competitive/Env check (owner: karthik_iyer)	- Ask CloudRetail which network egress point they measured from and whether an internal proxy added latency.

We should perform the no-batching reproduction first — that is the likeliest cause for the higher TTFT. If we replicate the numbers, we'll produce an ops note that explains behaviour and suggests mitigations (e.g., recommend enabling small prefix batching + edge-side aggregation to retain low TTFT while reducing cost).

Tentative plan to keep MAP timeline: run repro Thu 27, consolidated results Fri 28, short exec note Mon 30. I've linked the HubSpot deal and the shared Drive assets in the MAP doc.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference

Related: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/CR-2026-015
Attachment referenced: latency-results.csv (will upload after runs)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Simon Bryant <simon.bryant@cloudretail.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, nikhil_sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Benchmark plan, MAP milestones, and close timeline

Simon — quick update and MAP close plan. Thanks to Marissa, Nikhil and Grace for the fast triage. Summary of findings: 

- Reproduction: Nikhil ran the Redwood harness in three modes and reproduced the delta when the customer's proxy did not allow batching (1:1 calls). Our no-batching p50 = 160ms, p95 = 395ms which aligns closely with your edge measurement (great correlation).
- Root cause: the primary delta was tooling/config — your side measured edge-to-first-token including network proxy latency and no-batching semantics. Redwood's demo figures included an internal small-prefix batching profile which lowers p50 but can increase TTFT for single-request flows.
- Mitigations: 1) If UX requires strict p50 for single-request flows, we recommend enabling edge-side request aggregation or disabling batching for that route (we can configure per-route policies). 2) For cost tradeoffs, we propose a hybrid: allow small batching for background flows and dedicate an unbatched route for interactive endpoints.

Deliverables attached: final-results-summary.xlsx (includes side-by-side CSVs, traces, and a one-page MAP recommendation).

Next steps per MAP: 
- Procurement: proceed toward Go/No-Go with the Aug 31 exec readout.
- Technical: we will publish the per-route policy examples and a quick config guide by EOD Tue (Aug 31).
- Follow-up: Marissa will draft the ops note that explains behaviour for the execs and includes the recommended configuration.

If this aligns, consider the MAP closed for performance acceptance with the conditional policy decisions noted above.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: final-results-summary.xlsx (XLSX, 56 KB)
